headline: LEANING *FENCE?*
*3 USUAL CAUSES*
beats.vo: Fence leaning after the wind? It's usually one of three things.
One: rot. Wood posts rot first right at ground level, where wet soil meets air.
Two: shallow posts. A common rule of thumb is two to three feet deep for a six foot fence.

beats.label: 2X THE WIND = 4X THE PUSH
beats.vo: Three: soggy soil and wind. A solid fence catches wind like a sail, and twice the wind pushes four times as hard.

headline: PUSH ON
YOUR *POSTS*
beats.vo: After the first big storm, push on your posts. Wobble at ground level? Get it looked at.

beats.prompt: SEND THIS TO A FENCE OWNER
beats.vo: Send this to a fence owner.

post.caption: Leaning fence after a Lower Mainland windstorm? It's usually rot at ground level, posts set too shallow, or soggy soil plus wind on a solid fence. After the first big storm, push on your posts and check for wobble at the base.
post.alt: A stained cedar fence down a side yard, an animated diagram of a fence post rotting at ground level, and a new board-on-board cedar fence following a slope.
